figure_inventory.description: Black outline plus black dashed lines, white fill: a plus/cross shape made of 4 equal narrow rectangular arms (each arm about 25 px wide and about 90 px long beyond the central square) meeting at a small central square, so the whole cross is about 203 px tall and 203 px wide. A vertical dashed line and a horizontal dashed line pass through the centre along the middle of the arms and extend about 36 px beyond the arm ends on every side. In the upper-right quadrant a curved arrow starting on the horizontal dashed line (to the right of the centre) and ending on the vertical dashed line (above the centre), arrowhead at the vertical line, with the label '90 degrees' (written 90 with a small raised o) next to it.

A black-outline figure (no fill, white inside) built from two bands of equal width crossing at the centre, with thin black dashed lines through the middle of both bands. The dashed lines are one vertical and one horizontal line, each running a little beyond the figure on both ends and crossing in a small black dot at the centre of the figure. Horizontal band: straight, square ends, runs from the left edge to the right edge of the figure. Vertical band: the same length as the horizontal band, crossing it at the middle; its TOP end bends to the RIGHT: at the top an arm of the band width runs horizontally to the right and ends flush with the right end of the horizontal band (this top arm starts at the left edge of the vertical band, so it is a little more than half the band length). Its BOTTOM end bends to the LEFT in the same way: a horizontal arm of the band width at the bottom runs to the left and ends flush with the left end of the horizontal band. So the figure is like an S/Z with a horizontal bar through the middle: four arms, two plain (left, right) and two bent in opposite directions (top bends right, bottom bends left). The whole figure fits in a square; band width is about 1/8 of the band length. It looks the same after a half turn about the centre dot (2 angles of symmetry: 180 and 360 degrees).

NOTE: the three angles (about 90, 155, 115 degrees) are measured from the page picture; the book prints no values. Three radial arms, each a long narrow band (white inside, thin black outline, square ends) with a thin black dashed line down its middle, meeting at one point marked by a small bold black dot. The dashed centre lines run a tiny bit beyond each arm end. The three arms are about the same length but the angles between them are NOT equal: arm 1 points almost straight up (tilted about 5 degrees to the left of vertical); arm 2 points to the left, nearly horizontal (it dips about 5 degrees below horizontal); arm 3 points to the lower right (about 19 degrees below horizontal). Angles between neighbouring arms (measured from the picture): about 90 degrees (up arm to left arm), about 155 degrees (left arm to lower-right arm), about 115 degrees (lower-right arm back to up arm). No labels, no angle marks. The text says only a full turn of 360 degrees brings it back onto itself, so it has no rotational symmetry.

Three radial arms, each a long narrow band (white, black outline, square ends) with a thin black dashed line down its middle, meeting at the centre: one arm pointing straight up, one to the lower left, one to the lower right, equal length, drawn about 120 degrees apart. In each of the three gaps between neighbouring arms a small black circular arc is drawn around the centre to mark the angle, with a plain black letter beside it: A = gap between the up arm and the lower-right arm (arc on the right, letter A to the right of it, level with the upper part of the arc); B = gap between the lower-left arm and the lower-right arm (arc below the centre, letter B below it); C = gap between the up arm and the lower-left arm (arc on the left, letter C to the left of it). The second diagram printed to its right (P18-shape-2) is the same figure with the letters moved round.

Same three-arm figure as P18-shape-1 (arms pointing up, lower-left, lower-right, band outline with thin black dashed centre lines, a small arc in each gap) in the same position, but the letters are in different gaps: B = gap between the up arm and the lower-left arm (arc and letter B on the left); C = gap between the up arm and the lower-right arm (arc and letter C on the right); A = gap between the lower-left arm and the lower-right arm (arc and letter A below the centre). So the labelled gaps are those of the first diagram turned by one third of a full turn (A moved from the right gap to the bottom gap, B from the bottom gap to the left gap, C from the left gap to the right gap), which is what the text means by overlapping angle A with angle B, B with C, and C with A.

Four copies of the same equal-armed three-arm figure printed side by side in one row (each arm a long narrow band, black outline, square ends; arms pointing up, lower-left and lower-right, 120 degrees apart). Each arm has a coloured dashed line down its middle that runs a little past the arm end (colours: green, dark blue/indigo, red). Colours of the dashed lines (up arm / lower-left arm / lower-right arm): step 1 = green / blue / red; step 2 = red / green / blue; step 3 = blue / red / green; step 4 = green / blue / red (same as step 1). Captions under the steps: step 1 'Initial position'; step 2 'After 120 degrees rotation'; step 3 'After 240 degrees (120 degrees + 120 degrees) rotation'; step 4 'After 360 degrees (120 degrees + 120 degrees + 120 degrees) rotation' (3rd and 4th caption each run to three lines). Black curved arrows near the centre show the turn, each starting on the lower-right arm and going ANTICLOCKWISE: step 1 no arrow; step 2 a small arc of about 120 degrees from the lower-right arm up to the up arm, arrowhead at the up arm end; step 3 a larger arc of about 240 degrees (over the top to the lower-left arm), arrowhead at the lower-left arm; step 4 a full circle (360 degrees) round the centre with the arrowhead at the lower right. Below the row, an italic note: 'Note: The colours have been added to show the rotations.'

CORRECTED: the book's lower flag is not an exact half-turn copy of the upper flag (its tip hangs lower and further left); the book's answer (order 2) treats the figure as a half-turn pair, so it is drawn as an exact half-turn copy. A straight black line segment slanting from the upper left to the lower right (steep, about 58 degrees below horizontal) with a bold dot at its exact midpoint. At the UPPER-LEFT end a small triangular flag (open triangle outline) is attached: one side of the triangle lies along the line near the end and the triangle sticks out to the RIGHT of the line (its tip points right, almost level with the line end). At the LOWER-RIGHT end a small triangular flag is attached on the OPPOSITE (left/lower) side of the line: one side of the triangle lies along the line at the end and the tip points down and to the left, hanging a little below the line end. The two flags are on opposite sides of the line, like a half-turn pair, but they are not exact copies of each other.

NOTE: the arc marks only the top angle, which strictly breaks the 4-fold symmetry of the drawing; the book's answer (order 4) reads the arc as marking the right angle. Two black straight line segments of equal length crossing at their midpoints at right angles, drawn diagonally (like an X: one rising to the right, one falling to the right), with a bold dot at the crossing. A small black arc is drawn above the crossing point joining the two upper arms to mark the angle between them (the top angle of the X). No letter or value is printed on the arc.

A six-pointed star (hexagram outline, like two overlapping equilateral triangles drawn as one outline) in black, with 6 outer tips and 6 inner corners (12 corners in all). Tips point straight up, straight down, and to the upper-right, lower-right, lower-left and upper-left. A bold dot marks the centre.

A line drawing (thin black outline, white inside) of three identical human arms, each bent at the elbow, joined at the shoulder end in the middle of the figure and spreading out like a three-legged triskelion, 120 degrees apart. Each arm ends in a hand in a fist; hands are at the upper left (closed fist, facing up), at the upper right (fist seen from the side, pointing right) and at the bottom (fist pointing left-down). Each arm's upper part goes outward from the middle and its forearm turns round in the same direction (all three bends turn the same way). No centre dot is drawn.

A plus-sign/cross made of one vertical rectangle and one horizontal rectangle of equal size crossing in a central square whose four sides are drawn inside the cross (black outline, white inside). Each arm sticks out beyond the central square by about 1.4 times the square's side (each rectangle is about 3.8 times as long as it is wide). A bold dot marks the centre of the central square.
A regular pentagon with one vertex at the top and a flat horizontal side at the bottom (thick black outline, white inside), with a bold dot at its centre.

Figure (a): a straight slanted line segment from the upper-left to the lower-right (steep, about 60 degrees from the horizontal), with a small triangular flag attached at each end: at the top end the flag sits above the end of the line and points to the upper-right, at the bottom end it sits below the end of the line and points to the lower-left (the two flags are 180-degree rotations of each other). Label '(a)'. Answer line: 'order of symmetry=2'. Two rows of three figures separated by a thin horizontal rule between the rows; each figure has a letter label and a printed answer line under it.

Figure (b): two equal straight black line segments crossing at their midpoints, forming a wide X (the lines about 90 degrees apart, at 45 degrees to the page), with a small arc drawn across the upper angle (between the two upper arms) to mark the angle. Label '(b)'. Answer line: 'order of symmetry= 4'.

Figure (c): a six-pointed star outline (hexagram outline, 12 vertices: 6 outer points and 6 inner notches), one point straight up, black outline, no fill. Label '(c)'. Answer line: 'order of symmetry= 6'.

Figure (d): a line drawing of three human arms, each bent at the elbow and ending in a clenched fist, joined at the shoulders at a common centre in a triskelion arrangement (the three arms are the same drawing rotated by 120 degrees; one fist at the upper-left, one at the upper-right, one at the bottom). Thin black outline sketch, no fill. Label '(d)'. Answer line: 'order of symmetry= 3'.

Figure (e): a plus/cross shape drawn as two overlapping rectangles: a tall vertical rectangle (about 3.8 times as tall as wide) and a wide horizontal rectangle of the same size crossing in the middle, so the centre square is outlined with all four sides; a black dot at the centre of the centre square. Black outline, no fill. Label '(e)'. Answer line: 'order of symmetry= 4'.
Figure (f): a regular pentagon with a horizontal flat base and one vertex at the top, thick black outline, with a black dot at its centre. Label '(f)'. Answer line: 'order of symmetry= 5'.

Blue (single colour, thin black outlines) figure built only from equilateral triangles on a triangle grid, caption 'Pinwheel'. Centre: a regular hexagon made of 6 triangles meeting at one central point (hexagon corners at the top-left, top-right, right, bottom-right, bottom-left, left; slightly turned, not flat-topped). On each of the 6 sides of the hexagon one rhombus (two triangles joined along an edge) is stuck, so 12 outer triangles in 6 pairs; every rhombus is attached in the same turning sense so the whole figure looks like a six-bladed windmill. Total counted: 6 + 12 = 18 triangles. Overall the figure looks the same after a rotation of 60 degrees (6 positions) but no mirror line.

Five identical narrow wedge-shaped arms (long thin trapezoids, pointed/narrow at the centre and widening to a short flat end) all meeting at one centre point, spaced 72 degrees apart: one arm straight up, one to the upper-right (about 18 degrees above horizontal), one to the upper-left (same), one to the lower-right (about 54 degrees below horizontal) and one to the lower-left (same). Each arm is about 5 times as long as its flat end is wide. Black outline, no fill. Through each arm runs a dashed black line along its axis, extending a little beyond the flat end of the arm. Label '(a)' below the centre. Below the figure: 'Angles of symmetry = 72, 144, 216, 288, 360 (degrees)'.

Six identical lens-shaped petals (each pointed at both ends, bounded by two curved arcs), all meeting at one centre point (marked with a filled dot), spaced 60 degrees apart: one straight up, one straight down, and four at 30 degrees above and below the horizontal (upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right). Black outline, no fill. Through each petal runs a dashed line along its axis, extending slightly beyond the petal tip. Label '(b)' at the lower right. Below the figure: 'Angles of symmetry = 60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360 (degrees)'.

A circle (black outline, white inside) divided into 12 equal sectors by 12 black radii from the centre, 30 degrees apart (one radius straight up, one straight down, one to the left, one to the right and two more between each pair). No colour yet, no centre dot, no labels.

NOTE: the printed picture (4 adjacent shaded sectors) does not have 3 angles of symmetry although its caption says so; the LP solution (every 4th sector) is drawn instead. A circle divided into 12 equal sectors by 12 radii 30 degrees apart (one radius vertical up, one horizontal right, one horizontal left, one vertical down); black outlines; coloured sectors are filled raspberry/crimson-pink, the other sectors white. Figure (i): 4 adjacent sectors are shaded: the sectors between the radius pointing to the upper-left (120 degrees measured anticlockwise from the right-pointing radius) and the right-pointing horizontal radius (0 degrees), i.e. the sectors 120-90, 90-60, 60-30 and 30-0 degrees; the other 8 sectors are white. Caption under it: '(i) 3 Angles of Symmetry'.

NOTE: the printed picture (3 adjacent shaded sectors) does not have 4 angles of symmetry and its caption has no number; the LP solution (every 3rd sector) is drawn instead. A circle divided into 12 equal sectors by 12 radii 30 degrees apart (one radius vertical up, one horizontal right, one horizontal left, one vertical down); black outlines; coloured sectors are filled raspberry/crimson-pink, the other sectors white. Figure (ii): 3 adjacent sectors are shaded: the sectors 120-90, 90-60 and 60-30 degrees (from the upper-left radius to the radius 30 degrees above the right-pointing horizontal); the other 9 sectors are white. Caption under it: '(ii)  Angles of Symmetry' (no number printed).

A pencil-style black-and-grey illustration of a spoked bicycle wheel (seen slightly sideways so it looks a little oval, with a double rim and a hub made of concentric rings) sitting on a straight sloping line that goes down to the right. At the left end of the slope line a vertical line goes down from the top of the slope (a ramp). Short curved motion strokes are drawn at the left side and at the lower right of the wheel, and a thin straight stroke at the upper left, to show movement. About 16 thin spokes join the hub to the rim.

A picture of a ceiling fan seen from below, caption 'Fan' in italics under it: a round darker-blue hub in the middle and THREE light-blue rounded-rectangle blades radiating from it about 120 degrees apart (one blade pointing up and slightly left, one pointing right and slightly down, one pointing to the lower left). A thin light-blue curved arrow arc with an arrowhead is drawn round the hub (upper right) and another thin arc below the hub, showing the fan turning.

NOTE: the book's flower has SIX petals (the LP text and the teaching image say five). A flower with SIX yellow pointed-oval (leaf-shaped) petals with a thin dark outline, caption 'Flower' in italics under it. The petals point up, upper right, right, lower right/bottom, lower left and left, all turned the same way like a pinwheel so that each petal partly overlaps the next near the centre; where they overlap near the centre there are thin red-orange slivers.

NOTE: the book's wheel has 23 spokes (the teaching image shows 8). A circle (thin black outline) with 23 thin straight black spokes drawn from the centre to the rim (counted by eye and again by sampling a circle round the centre: 23), caption 'Wheel' in italics under it. One spoke points straight up; the spokes are spaced about 15.65 degrees apart (360/23), so there is NO spoke straight down and no two spokes are exactly opposite each other.
